title: Penile and Adrenal Cancers: High-Yield Essentials

steps.tx: Penile epithelial malignancy arises via two distinct pathogeneses and viral associations. **Penile squamous cell carcinoma** is associated with human papillomavirus HPV infection in 40% to 50% of cases, primarily spreading sequentially to superficial and deep **inguinal lymph nodes**. Non-HPV-associated carcinomas develop from chronic inflammatory conditions including lichen sclerosus, showing high rates of somatic TP53 alterations and p16INK4a negativity.
steps.say: Penile epithelial malignancy arises via two distinct pathogeneses and viral associations. Penile squamous cell carcinoma is associated with human papillomavirus HPV infection in 40% to 50% of cases, primarily spreading sequentially to superficial and deep inguinal lymph nodes. Non-HPV carcinomas develop from chronic inflammation, showing somatic TP53 alterations.

right.title: HPV-Negative Penile Cancer
points: Associated with phimosis and lichen sclerosus
Frequent TP53 mutations and poorer prognosis

steps.tx: Accurate nodal staging determines long-term curability in invasive penile malignancy. Dynamic **sentinel lymph node biopsy** or modified bilateral **inguinal lymphadenectomy** is indicated for intermediate- and high-risk invasive primary tumours (T1G2 or higher) to detect occult micrometastases. Because lymphatic drainage follows an orderly progression from superficial to deep inguinal nodes, radical inguinal lymphadenectomy provides decisive regional staging and curative disease control.

steps.tx: Bulky or fixed inguinal nodal disease requires multimodality downstaging prior to extirpative surgery. **Neoadjuvant combination chemotherapy** with **TIP** combining **paclitaxel**, **ifosfamide**, and **cisplatin** achieves objective response rates of 50% to 55% in fixed, unresectable inguinal adenopathy. Delivering 4 cycles of neoadjuvant TIP induces significant tumour cytoreduction, converting inoperable fixed nodal masses into completely resectable specimens with clear surgical margins.

steps.tx: Endocrine cortical neoplasms display distinctive autonomous hormone excess syndromes. **Adrenocortical carcinoma** is an aggressive endocrine malignancy presenting with functional hormone excess in **60%** of patients, most frequently manifesting as rapid-onset **Cushing syndrome** or virilisation from excessive adrenal androgen secretion. Autonomous hypercortisolemia is accompanied by elevated serum DHEAS, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and loss of normal diurnal cortisol rhythm requiring formal biochemical evaluation.

steps.tx: The coronal and axial views show a bulky left upper abdominal mass with a dark dead center sitting above a pushed down kidney. This is **adrenocortical carcinoma** with **central necrosis**, the classic large heterogeneous tumor that displaces nearby organs. Many such cancers secrete excess cortisol or androgens causing **Cushing syndrome** or virilisation. Size plus heterogeneity and necrosis on imaging should raise concern for carcinoma over benign adenoma.
steps.say: This image shows a large left adrenal cancer with a necrotic center pushing the left kidney downward. The mass is bulky and uneven in texture, typical of adrenocortical carcinoma rather than a small smooth adenoma. These cancers often produce excess cortisol or androgens, so patients may present with rapid weight gain, hypertension, or virilisation alongside the mass. A large heterogeneous adrenal lesion with necrosis deserves full hormone testing and surgical evaluation.

steps.tx: Histological distinction between benign adenomas and malignant carcinomas requires multiparameter scoring. The **Weiss histopathological score** predicts malignancy in **adrenocortical neoplasms** by evaluating nine distinct microscopic criteria. Features include mitotic rate greater than 5 per 50 high-power fields, atypical mitotic figures, venous invasion, sinusoidal invasion, capsular invasion, necrosis, nuclear pleomorphism, and low clear cell architecture. A Weiss score of **3** or greater establishes the definitive diagnosis of carcinoma.

steps.tx: Histology alone cannot separate benign from malignant adrenal tumours. The **Weiss criteria** assess nine histological features, and a score of **three or more** features suggests malignancy. Malignant adrenal cortical tumours are then managed by the features above. In pheochromocytoma, malignancy is defined by metastases rather than microscopic appearance. Mutations in the **SDHB** gene carry a higher risk of malignant behaviour in paragangliomas.

steps.tx: Targeted adrenocortical adrenolysis forms the foundation of adjuvant medical management. **Mitotane** is an **adrenolytic agent** used in adjuvant and metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma, requiring plasma concentration monitoring to maintain therapeutic levels between 14 and 20 mg/L. Because mitotane selectively destroys adrenal cortical mitochondria while strongly inducing hepatic CYP3A4, concurrent high-dose replacement hydrocortisone is mandatory to prevent acute adrenal crisis.

nodes.label: Maintain Serum Level Between 14 and 20 mg/L

steps.tx: Metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma demands aggressive combination cytotoxic therapy paired with oral adrenolytics. The international FIRM-ACT trial established **EDP-mitotane** combining **etoposide**, **doxorubicin**, and **cisplatin** with mitotane as the global first-line standard for advanced adrenocortical carcinoma, demonstrating superior response rates and progression-free survival compared to streptozocin regimens. Mitotane-mediated CYP3A4 induction requires escalated doses of replacement corticosteroids throughout cytotoxic administration.

The international FIRM-ACT trial established EDP-mitotane combining etoposide, doxorubicin, and cisplatin with mitotane as the first-line standard for advanced adrenocortical carcinoma, demonstrating superior response rates and progression-free survival compared to streptozocin regimens.

left.title: EDP-Mitotane (FIRM-ACT Standard)
points: Objective response rate 23.2% vs 9.2% for streptozocin
Established first-line global standard of care

right.title: Endocrine Supportive Measures
points: Accelerates clearance of hydrocortisone and dexamethasone
Requires 2 to 3 times standard replacement steroid doses
Monitor urinary free cortisol and ACTH levels

steps.tx: Neural crest chromaffin tissue malignancies display genetic predispositions to metastatic dissemination. **Malignant pheochromocytomas** and paragangliomas are defined by metastatic spread to non-chromaffin sites like bone and liver, strongly associated with germline **SDHB mutations** in succinate dehydrogenase subunit B. Loss of succinate dehydrogenase activity leads to intracellular succinate accumulation, inhibiting prolyl hydroxylases and pseudo-hypoxic HIF-1-alpha stabilization that drives metastatic vascular spread.
